row.evidence: Nutshell's help centre says SSO and directory sync (DS) are available on the Sales Enterprise plan, with at least 10 licenses required to set up DS, but it never says which protocol DS uses and no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New in 2026-09. Status unknown rather than gated: Enterprise ($79/user/mo billed annually, $89 monthly) includes SAML SSO (5-license minimum) and an admin-portal 'directory sync' (10-license minimum, SSO required first) that creates users from an external directory as unlicensed, syncs name and email changes, and strips licenses when the directory user is deleted; it syncs every 15 minutes. Nutshell never says whether DS is SCIM or a vendor-run directory pull, no SCIM endpoint, token or IdP provisioning guide is published, and the Okta OIN app is SWA only, so SCIM cannot be confirmed. If DS proves to be SCIM, the row becomes gated at Enterprise. Tiers (annual / monthly per user): Foundation $13/$19, Growth $25/$32, Pro $42/$49, Business $59/$67, Enterprise $79/$89; plan names come from the cards' 'Everything in X' lines and the page's structured data. Audit log is in-app only (Business and Enterprise, not exportable). The REST API only reads users (GET /users, GET /users/{id}); the legacy JSON-RPC API has newUser, editUser, deleteUser and findUsers; the plan needed for API keys is not stated. Google Apps users can also sync into Nutshell.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price_text: $79 per user, per month billed annually ($89 monthly)
plans.notes: Enterprise SSO (5-license minimum) and directory sync (10-license minimum, protocol undisclosed); read-only SQL access.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint, token or IdP provisioning guide is documented. Enterprise 'directory sync' automates create, update and license removal from an external directory, but its protocol is not disclosed, so available stays null.

deprovision.data_retained: Directory sync: a user deleted in the external directory becomes Nutshell-managed and loses their Nutshell licenses. Manual removal: removed users cannot log in and their historical data persists.
deprovision.notes: Describes Enterprise directory sync, whose protocol is undisclosed.

limitations.text: Directory sync (Enterprise) needs SSO configured first, at least 10 licenses, and SSO needs a custom domain; DS-created users start unlicensed and must be licensed in Nutshell before they can log in; emails are only ever added, never removed.
Admins cannot remove directory-sync-managed users in Nutshell; they must be removed in the synced directory. Sync runs at setup and every 15 minutes.

user_api.notes: Two APIs: the REST API (current) only reads users; the legacy JSON-RPC API at https://app.nutshell.com/api/v1/json (no new endpoints being added) can create, edit, delete and find users and teams.

auth.notes: HTTP Basic: a user's email (or company domain for JSON-RPC) as username, API key from Settings > API keys as password.

capabilities.notes: Create, edit and delete are JSON-RPC only; manage_groups = JSON-RPC Team methods.

endpoints.purpose: JSON-RPC newUser: Create a new User
JSON-RPC findUsers: Find users matching a query
JSON-RPC newTeam: Create a new Team

audit_log_api.notes: Audit log is in-app only on Business and Enterprise and cannot be downloaded or exported.

rate_limits.text: JSON-RPC: large find requests with non-stub responses and excessive get requests are rate limited; no numeric limit published.

okta.notes: OIN 'Nutshell' app (last updated Jan. 21 2022) marks only SWA (read from page markup).

entra.notes: Nutshell's SSO setup lists Entra ID; no Entra gallery tutorial (nutshell-tutorial 404). Whether directory sync works with Entra is not stated.

google.notes: Nutshell's SSO setup lists Google Workspace; separately, a Google Apps integration syncs users into Nutshell.

fallbacks.other_sync: Enterprise directory sync from an external directory (protocol undisclosed); Google Apps user sync
